newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan Diesel to double capital spending in 3 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Nissan Diesel to double capital spending in 3 yrs.

text.p: Nissan Diesel Motor Co Ltd said on Wednesday it planned to double its capital investment in the three years from April 1 compared with the previous three-year period.
The move is to cope with the planned introduction of tighter emission regulations.

Nissan Diesel president Masayuki Saito also told reporters the company planned to start mass-production of its "Asia Truck" -- an Asian-made truck to be sold under the Nissan Diesel brand name in the Asian market -- early this year.
Saito also said Nissan Diesel wanted the yen to stay at its current level against the dollar.
Nissan Diesel, owned 39.8 percent by Nissan Motor Co Ltd, produces trucks and buses.

Saito said the company planned to increase capital investment to an annual average of 15 billion to 16 billion yen in the three years from 1997/98, compared with an average eight billion yen in between 1994/95 and 1996/97.

The Asia Truck will be assembled in Indonesia, Malaysia, Pakistan and Thailand from 1997, using parts made in those countries, Saito said. It will be sold in the four countries under the Nissan Diesel brand name.
